Target: a discrete-time model

target_discrete.Rd

Builds the target of an analysis whose follow-up is recorded in intervals \(1, \dots, K\) (years, visits, treatment cycles): subject \(i\) is at risk in intervals \(1, \dots, t_i\) and, when its event indicator is 1, has the event in interval \(t_i\). The model is the grouped-time (discrete-time) model of the interval hazards, $$h_k(z) = P(T = k \mid T \ge k, z) = g^{-1}(\gamma_{sk} + z^\top\beta),$$ with one baseline parameter \(\gamma_{sk}\) for each stratum \(s\) and interval \(k\), and the link \(g\) set by link. The target sets the likelihood \(\ell(\theta)\) in the objective of cv.bregsurv(): the Bernoulli log-likelihood of every subject's intervals at risk.

target_discrete() checks your data and stores it; it fits nothing. Pass the result to cv.bregsurv() (or bregsurv()) as target.

Usage

target_discrete(
  interval,
  event,
  z,
  stratum = NULL,
  link = c("cloglog", "logit"),
  n_intervals = NULL,
  score = "linear"
)

Arguments

interval

The last interval each subject was at risk in, a whole number from 1 to \(K\): the interval of the event for a subject with the event, and the last interval completed without it for a censored subject.

event

Event indicator of each subject: 1 if the event happened in interval interval, 0 if the subject was censored after it. Coded as the event of target_cox().

z

Covariates, one row per subject and one named column per covariate, as for target_cox().

stratum

Optional stratum of each subject, any labels. Each stratum has its own baseline parameters \(\gamma_{sk}\); the coefficients are shared.

link

The link \(g\):

  • "cloglog" (the default), the complementary log-log, \(h_k(z) = 1 - \exp\{-\exp(\gamma_{sk} + z^\top\beta)\}\): the grouped proportional-hazards model, whose coefficients are log hazard ratios, as a Cox model's are, so they compare directly with a Cox model's coefficients;

  • "logit", \(\log\{h_k / (1 - h_k)\} = \gamma_{sk} + z^\top\beta\): proportional odds of the interval hazard.

n_intervals

The number of intervals \(K\); defaults to max(interval). Set it when the external model covers later intervals that none of your subjects reached.

score

The form of the risk score: "linear" (the default), or a neural network specified by nn_score() that outputs one logit per interval (requires the torch package; the Kullback-Leibler divergence only, the logit link, and no strata).

Value

An object of class "bregsurv_target", a list with

type

"discrete".

interval, event, stratum

The checked intervals, event indicators and strata.

z

The covariates as a numeric matrix with column names.

link, K, score

The link, the number of intervals and the form of the risk score.

n

The number of subjects.

See also

cv.bregsurv(); the other targets, target_cox() and target_ncc(); the releases, release_records(), release_coef(), release_score() and release_model().

Examples

data(ExampleData_discrete)
dt <- ExampleData_discrete$train
table(last_interval = dt$interval, event = dt$status)
#>              event
#> last_interval  0  1
#>             1 27  7
#>             2 21 12
#>             3 21  3
#>             4 19  6
#>             5 20  3
#>             6 10  1
target_discrete(interval = dt$interval, event = dt$status, z = dt$z)
#> Target: discrete-time model, 6 intervals, cloglog link
#>   150 subjects, 6 covariates, 32 events
